subject: Bug fix to stratified uppass calculations and fixnode calculations

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Bug fix to stratified uppass calculations and fixnode calculations
parts:
Dear BioGeoBEARS users,

1. Fix to uppass calculations in stratified analyses: Awhile
back, I posted a fix to the uppass calculations, which are a
(usually minor) part of the calculation of ancestral range
probabilities.

I thought my fix also covered the stratified calculations,
but thanks to Julien I figured out what was left out. I've
uploaded fixed code for the stratified calculations. As
with the other fix, this won't change likelihoods, the root
states, model choices, or probably most of the ancestral
range estimates, but it might change ancestral range
estimates a bit above the root and on corners.

2. Also, for fans of the fixnode/fixlikes option (basically
Julien!), which lets you fix the ranges at particular nodes,
e.g. for hypothesis testing by comparing likelihoods under
different ancestral range hypotheses:

I have now ensured that when likelihoods of the different
states/ranges are fixed at certain nodes, these are
multiplied in applied during uppass calculations at that
node. Previously, the fixed likelihoods were only used on
downpass calculations. I thought initially it wouldn't
matter, because multiplying by e.g. c(0, 1, 0, 0) in the
downpass will also ensure c(0, 1, 0, 0) at that node in the
final state probabilities, no matter what the uppass
probabilities are. But it *does* matter for the corners just
above that node. Normally you wouldn't be able to tell
anyway, but if you do something radical, e.g. fix a node to
be region "A" when all the tips above it are region "B", the
different matters. I have made this change for both
stratified and non-stratified analyses.


As before, you can get the fixes from PhyloWiki, with:

================================
library(BioGeoBEARS)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_classes_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stratified_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_univ_model_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_readwrite_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wikidot.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_loglike_sp_v01.R")
calc_loglike_sp = compiler::cmpfun(calc_loglike_sp_prebyte)
# crucial to fix bug in uppass calculations
================================


Other minor updates made:

BioGeoBEARS_classes_v1.R -- narrowed the default min/max for
d and e, hopefully to prevent the presumed underflow issue
causing crashes on some machines (usually Windows)

All optim() and optimx() searches with bears_optim_run() now
run a "test likelihood calculation". If this crashes due to
poor inputs or whatever, it will spit out a more useful
error than you get when the crash happens inside of optim()
or optimx().

Minor improvements to the plot function.

Various improvements/cleanup/added documentation for the of
the example script:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#toc14

Note that I have changed the names of the "DIVA" and
"BAYAREA" models to "DIVALIKE" and "BAYAREALIKE", as they
are really likelihood interpretations of parsimony DIVA and
Bayesian BayArea, not exact replicates. This was fairly
obvious from the get-go, but it's good to be clear!

Thanks everyone for sharing issues when they arise, it does
make the package better!

Cheers,
Nick
